newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $61-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $61-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade Wednesday was slow at $61.00-$61.50 per cwt, down $0.50 to $1.00 from Tuesday's top, feedlot sources said.
About 7,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date figure near 106,500, they said.
An estimated 700 head sold in Kansas, which brought the weekly figure near 75,000, the sources said.
Most of the showlist in the Panhandle and about 80 percent of the list in Kansas was sold, the feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle sales at $61.00 were down $2.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, with owners losing an average of $60.00 to $65.00 per head, several cattle sources said.
Prices were pressured by lower beef values and the need for feedlots to remain current, they said.

Feedlots have to remain current to avoid a buildup of surplus supplies following heavy placements of cattle onto feedlots last spring. Those cattle are now being finished out and will be coming to market the next three to four weeks, the cattlemen said.
